generalizedRange: Rivers, estuaries and coasts of Europe and the Mediterranean, from Scandinavia to North Africa; spawns far out in the western Atlantic
hook: It crosses the Atlantic twice and eats nothing on the way home.

story.text: Every European eel begins in the Sargasso Sea, a breeding ground deduced from larvae a century ago and never yet seen.
Transparent, leaf-shaped larvae drift some 4,000 miles to Europe, arriving after a year or two as finger-length glass eels.
In rivers they darken into yellow eels and stay five to twenty years, hunting by night.
Then the body rebuilds: skin silvers, eyes grow up to ten times larger, the gut shuts down, and the eel leaves to spawn once and die.
Only in 2022 did satellite tags give direct evidence: of 26 silver eels released off the Azores, five reached the Sargasso, one the presumed breeding area.
Meanwhile the young stopped coming: glass-eel arrivals around the North Sea stand near 1 percent of the 1960–1979 average, around a tenth elsewhere in Europe.
Between river and sea stand weirs and turbines, and smugglers who move around 100 tonnes of glass eels a year to Asian farms — Europe’s largest wildlife crime, says the European Commission.
Critically Endangered since 2008, it draws the same advice from ICES every year: zero catch, every habitat, every life stage.
To witness the European eel is to follow a life that spans an ocean twice — and to keep the river open for the last crossing.

stats.size: Usually 2–2.6 ft · 2–4 lbs; exceptionally up to 5 ft
stats.lifespan: Around 20 years on average, up to 50; possibly longer if landlocked
stats.diet: Nocturnal predator & scavenger — fish, molluscs, crustaceans, carrion

reproduction.text: Each eel spawns once, in the Sargasso Sea, and then dies; the larvae that hatch there take a year or two to drift to Europe, and no one has yet seen the spawning itself.

insight.text: Before it leaves for the Sargasso Sea, a silver eel’s eyes grow up to ten times their original size and its digestive tract shuts down — it will never eat again.

programs.title: Eel passes and screens, England
programs.summary: Builds and monitors eel passes at weirs and sluices under the Eels (England and Wales) Regulations 2009 — two new passes on the Warwickshire Avon reopened 26.7 km of river in 2023, part of improvements secured at around 1,000 sites across England.

programs.title: Gannel Estuary eel project, Cornwall
programs.summary: Since 2022, with Newquay Marine Group, Cormac and the Environment Agency, evaluates the eels using the Gannel estuary and its catchment, has installed a mussel-rope eel pass to help glass eels move upstream, and is planning video and catch monitoring of barriers to migration.
